title: asymmetry-aware-kernel-dispatch-and-kv-compactor-for-llama-mistral-qwen
author: Nora Patel
description:
Motivation: We see a recurring class of tail-latency and throughput regressions for models with asymmetric per-head compute patterns (LLama variants with fused heads and older Mistral checkpoints that expose uneven head widths). Qwen long-context runs also expose hot paths where a single heavy head causes kernel selection thrash and excessive KV memory churn. This PR introduces two coordinated runtime features: 1) an Asymmetry-Aware Kernel Dispatch (AAKD) that classifies attention workloads at the request prelude and pins them to a small palette of specialized kernels (fast-path, wide-head, narrow-head) to avoid repeated kernel switching under mixed workloads; 2) a KV Compactor and scheduler that maintains compacted KV slabs for contiguous active prefix regions and schedules eviction/compaction tasks opportunistically during cross-request idle windows. Together these reduce kernel dispatch overhead, reduce KV fragmentation, and improve steady-state throughput for mixed-model fleets.

Design summary: AAKD performs a lightweight head-profile analysis when the first attention step is seen (O(1) sampling of head dims and sparsity flags). Profiles are hashed to a 32-bit signature and looked up in a small adaptive cache that maps signatures to kernel hints (vector-of-kernel-ids + expected token-cost). The kernel picker is conservative: it prefers a single specialized kernel when the signature confidence is high, otherwise falls back to the generic fused kernel. The KV Compactor maintains per-worker prioritized slabs for recently used prefixes. Compaction is backgrounded and has a throttled budget; it merges adjacent small KV allocations when a prefix becomes cold and collapses redundant host-to-device transfers for hot segments. The scheduler exposes a tunable policy (latency-first | throughput-first | balanced) and integrates with the continuous-batcher so that compaction can be deferred until batch drain points.

Compatibility and model quirks: Implemented compatibility rules for known quirks: (a) Llama variants with head fusion markers now prefer the narrow-head kernel when fusion flag present; (b) older Mistral checkpoints that report variable head widths are forced through a normalization pass that augments profile signatures to avoid oscillation; (c) Qwen long-context runs with hybrid rotary/fixed pos encoders are profiled to avoid prefetching entire KV slabs for early prefixes. Tests include explicit reproducers built from customer traces where oscillation previously caused 12–18% higher p99 latency.

Benchmarks: Microbenchmarks run on p4d-like machines (simulated in infra): - Mixed Llama + Mistral MQA workload: throughput +9.8% (tokens/s) and p99 -14% vs main. - Qwen long-context (32k) synthetic replay: token throughput +6.2%, median latency -11%. - Steady-state KV memory usage down by ~18% on average due to compaction and merged transfers. Real-customer canary on Dedicated pool (small cohort) showed no quality regressions; end-to-end application latency and cost-per-token improved for heavier head-mix apps.

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag asym_kv_compact and runtime_kdispatch. Default rollout: disabled on hosted API, enabled in Dedicated for selected customers via console toggle, opt-in for Private via config. Canary included: route policy for 5% traffic across two customer tenants running Llama/Mistral mixtures. Observability: new metrics: asd.kernel_hint, asd.signature_miss_rate, kv.compaction_ops, kv.slab_frag_pct, kv.compaction_latency. Added alerting defaults for anomalous compaction latency (>200ms) and signature churn (>20% within 10m).

Testing: Unit tests for signature hashing and kernel mapping, integration tests for compactor correctness, stress harness that replays mixed-head traces for 48h. Perf tests included in CI (perf/bench_asym_dispatch.py). Backwards compatibility tests verify that old checkpoints without metadata still pick fallback kernels.

Implementation notes: Major changes concentrated in runtime/dispatch and runtime/kv. No public API changes. Configurable knobs added in serving/config/runtime.toml. Documentation: docs/notes/asym_kernels.md and examples/recipes/llama-mistral-qwen-compat.yaml provide guidance for ops teams. Security: no user data exfiltration; compactor runs entirely in-worker process.

Open items: - Need a follow-up to tune budget heuristics for very high throughput Dedicated pools (ENG-2102). - Consider integrating signature signals with optimizer for adaptive quant profiles (investigation item).

release_notes: Introduce asymmetry-aware kernel dispatch to reduce kernel switching overhead for mixed-head models (opt-in)
Add KV Compactor to lower KV fragmentation and host-device transfer costs (background compaction, configurable budget)
New runtime flags: asym_kv_compact, runtime_kdispatch; observability metrics for kernel hints and compaction
No model output quality changes expected; feature is gated and disabled by default on hosted API
